asr.full_text: Welcome back to The Defiant. Today we're diving into the tokenomics of Polkadot, exploring the use cases, economic structure and staking mechanisms behind the DOT token. In order to build digital economies at scale, most networks rely on incentivization and validation methods through their native tokens. However, tokens are often only as strong as the economics behind them, often referred to as tokenomics. Properly balanced tokenomics can determine both the success and failure of these ecosystems. The polkadot network and all of its parachains are powered by the DOT token. While its utilities vary, the primary use cases for DOT include transaction and payment costs on the network, ecosystem governance, and bootstrapping the launch of new parachains. DOT is currently the 21st-ranked token by market capitalization and touts a $6 billion valuation. The token hit its all-time high in November 2021, soaring past $53 per cent. However, like much of the altcoin market, its price has since pulled back. DOT currently is trading at around $4 per cent, and is up nearly 4% over the last two weeks. The DOT token is finely tuned to ensure that various ecosystem components, such as staking, are balanced out by it's inflation system. DOT's inflation schedule is currently set at 10% annually, which means that the tokens supply increases by 10% every year. The newly minted tokens are split amongst DOT stakers and the polkadot treasury However with the recent passing of polkadot referendum 1139 The inflation rate is set to be reduced to 8% While also establishing a standardized fixed treasury flow The amount of DOT staked which can also be referred to as the ideal staking rate represents the other end of the spectrum for DOT tokenomics The balance between inflation and the amount of DOTs staked is what allows the tokenomics to stay in equilibrium. DOT's staking mechanics and inflation models are designed to work together to promote economic stability. Polkadot implements a nominated proof-of-stake design, which consists of validators and nominators. Validators are responsible for block production and finality, while nominators leverage their stake to back-select validators when necessary and approve trusted candidates. As of August Polkadot has 297 active validators and almost 37k nominators, with a historical rewards of 16.8%. The inflation rate is designed to incentivize dot holders to stake their dot whenever the staking rate is less than what is referred to as the ideal staking rate. This system works both ways and it also disincentivizes staking when it is greater than the ideal staking rate. This balance between staking rewards treasury rewards and the ideal staking rate is what creates the DOT inflation model and drives the DOT economy. Thank you again for tuning in today and remember to stay Defiant. 🎵
